evidence.summary: 独立 AI 桌面办公客户端，以多轮模型和本机工具执行文件、命令及报告任务，提供审批、运行记录和可选沙箱。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 package.json、README.md、electron/main.cjs、src/components/chat/ChatView.tsx、src/core/agent/agentLoopRunner.ts、sidecar/src/agentLoopHost.ts、src/core/agent/agentLoop.ts、src/core/agent/toolExecutor.ts、src/core/tools/registry.ts、src/core/permissions/permissionMode.ts、src/core/tools/definitions/commandTools.ts、src/core/sandbox/config.ts、electron/commandHost.cjs、electron/sandbox-launcher/src/main.rs、electron/secretStore.cjs、src/core/llm/openai-compatible.ts、src/core/session/checkpoint.ts、src/core/agent/loopGuards.ts、src/stores/settingsStore.ts；Electron dispatch到sidecar同agent loop，模型tool calls经审批/执行后结果回模型；终态/权限和平台Host分层。见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
limitations: 无旧稿/旧findings/依赖可读。当前核package/Electron主入口和ChatView→dispatch→sidecar共用loop、轮数/停止、toolExecutor/registry部分审批/结果路径、模式、commandTools/Host Seatbelt/proxy和Windows token/Job、Electron secretStore与OpenAI adapter/checkpoint。未全审4k行runner、全部registry、所有浏览器/CU/插件/MCP、后台/IM/多Agent或全部日志/迁移，不执行目标。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: 为希望自然语言驱动本机办公任务的人，提供模型连续决策、工具执行和成果界面。见[Q01](#research-q01)。
Electron dispatch到sidecar同agent loop，模型tool calls经审批/执行后结果回模型；终态/权限和平台Host分层。见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。

无旧稿/旧findings/依赖可读。当前核package/Electron主入口和ChatView→dispatch→sidecar共用loop、轮数/停止、toolExecutor/registry部分审批/结果路径、模式、commandTools/Host Seatbelt/proxy和Windows token/Job、Electron secretStore与OpenAI adapter/checkpoint。未全审4k行runner、全部registry、所有浏览器/CU/插件/MCP、后台/IM/多Agent或全部日志/迁移，不执行目标。
abu0.60.1、Apache-2.0独立Electron应用，main electron/main.cjs；DSH目录引用不改变client类型，目标发布/签名/运行兼容未独立验证。
Electron/sidecar/native/模型与权限/副本为底座，浏览器/MCP按任务另需；表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
模型/工具与复核恢复成本未知；默认200轮、非正配置可无限，正有限轮数仍非总费用或时间上限，须观察实际用量；表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
能验产物、读回有效正有限轮数并观察资源的人可standard副本小样；超人工阈值、越界或Stop后状态未知时停扩权/重试，核真实文件/请求再恢复。见[Q05](#research-q05)。
真实执行/权限/记录有据，办公正确率/净时间、全工具保密和恢复效果未测；表见[Q05](#research-q05)。
sidecar同审批、allow后abort/文件再核与secret持久错误可见可借鉴；平台profile、前台detach与记录持久边界须共同传给业务终态。见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
真实自主工具闭环及sidecar/审批/结果持久化接线，支持用户检查过程；未证明替代人工或净节时。见[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02)。
显式非正maxTurns可无限，轮数非总费用上限；Stop可先detach不等副作用已停，平台沙箱/代理需实况，远端模型接收上下文，记录非业务验收。见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
未验证方向是已有run/快照上新增成果验收与未知在途收据，比较误完成/重复动作/恢复工时，现机制已足够则否定。见[Q06](#research-q06)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)已有桌面Agent模式整合novelty小幅9；[Q02](#research-q02)sidecar/真实闭环与审批后再核实质mechanism15，非新模型算法23；[Q03](#research-q03)授权/平台条件和[Q04](#research-q04)秘密失败传播可条件迁移10；办公交接简化8但配置/验收仍重非12。 [Q02](#research-q02)默认轮数有护栏但支持显式无限，不计为普遍有限或总成本控制；闭环与授权贡献仍成立，数值保留。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)聊天建议转实际多步办公交付实质workflow18；[Q02](#research-q02)文件/结果与记录交付实质15但合格率无证据到23；独立桌面入口reach小幅5；[Q05](#research-q05)模型/人工总费未测，economics未识别0。

recommendation.reason: 希望自然语言驱动本机办公且能复核成果的桌面用户，可在 standard 权限、副本目录和读回的有效正有限轮数下试只读报告及一次可逆写入。它比纯聊天多真实工具闭环、审批与记录，但非正轮数可无限且轮数不封顶总费用，平台隔离和 Stop 后动作也须另核。达到人工时间或用量阈值、结果不符、越界或停止后状态不明时，应停扩权和重复执行，人工核文件、进程及外部请求并从副本恢复。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)ChatView到真实多轮工具链与办公副本任务具体，超泛用途15；持续需求/手工替代不足未对照，不到30。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)真实执行/结果回流和审批再核超只有聊天UI6；[Q03](#research-q03)平台边界及[Q05](#research-q05)结果/恢复未验证，未到19。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)真实sidecar同循环、[Q02](#research-q02)真实helper/继续回流与停因、[Q03](#research-q03)Host实际调用launcher/缺失拒绝及[Q04](#research-q04)秘密网络直接核超片段6；没运行、非全安全审计或实际有限费用证明，不到19。

cost.rationale: [Q05](#research-q05)模型/权限/平台和中断后核真实状态负担重要；[Q02](#research-q02)默认200但显式非正无限、正值不验Finite且轮数不封顶费用，须读回正有限配置并观察资源，工时费用未知；可回退副本小样非0，未到10。

publication.summaries.text: 独立 AI 桌面办公客户端，以多轮模型和本机工具执行文件、命令及报告任务，提供审批、运行记录和可选沙箱。

items.界面: 独立桌面办公/执行与成果界面
items.模型工具: 本机文件/命令、可选MCP和浏览器执行
items.Agent/Preset: 多轮自主模型工具循环与方法配置
items.后台: 可选调度/IM等产品面，本轮未全审

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 自主执行 | 模型选工具→结果回流继续 | 真Agent，最终成果仍验收 |
| 文件/命令 | 本机办公产物 | 审批/OS条件分层，Stop非全副作用回滚 |
| 权限/隔离 | 模式/路径/平台限制 | Win/mac不同，proxy port与豁免另核 |
| 密钥/记录 | safeStorage及运行/结果线索 | 非所有数据加密/绝对离线或exactly-once |
| 可选外部工具 | MCP/浏览器/后台任务 | 本轮只核部分边界，不能泛推全部安全 |

publication.advice.text: 能验产物、读回有效正有限轮数并观察资源的人可standard副本小样；超人工阈值、越界或Stop后状态未知时停扩权/重试，核真实文件/请求再恢复。见[Q05](#research-q05)。

width=\"60%\" /></td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n## Features\n\n### Core Capabilities\n\n- **Autonomous Agent** — More than chat: plans, invokes tools, reads/writes files, executes commands, and completes complex tasks end-to-end\n- **Plan Mode** — For high-risk steps (delete / overwrite / send / install), Abu first presents a step-by-step plan and waits for you to click \"Confirm & run\"; only read-only ops run while awaiting approval\n- **Interactive questions** — When Abu needs you to decide (pick an approach, provide a parameter), it pops an option card above the composer; single or multi-select, with an \"Other\" free-text row\n- **Per-conversation settings** — Permission mode (Request Approval / Smart Review / Full Autonomy) and model can be switched per conversation without bleeding across chats\n- **Soul Personality System** — Three proactivity presets (Quiet / Buddy / Butler) decide when Abu speaks up; customize tone, address, reply style, and boundaries via `SOUL.md`\n- **Self-Evolving Skills** — After you run a multi-step complex flow, Abu proactively offers \"want to crystallize this into a skill?\" — one click drafts it, you review, you accept. Next time, just name the skill; no need to re-explain\n- **Smart Notification System** — Menubar unread count / sidebar badge / system notification auto-routed; notices queued to inbox while you're in fullscreen / DnD, surfaced via badges once you're back; audit trail kept for 180 days\n- **Projects** — Promote a workspace into a Project: conversations in the same direction auto-aggregate; each project gets its own default model, skill set, and MCP connectors\n- **Multi-Agent Parallel Execution** — Run up to 5 background agents simultaneously, each executing tasks independently with real-time progress tracking\n- **Desktop Pet** (Labs) — Transparent floating window; left-click opens main window, right-click menu, drag-to-edge dock; **activity tray** shows Abu's live status (working / awaiting approval / done) and lets you reply inline while it waits\n- **Theme switching** — Light / dark / system, via Settings → Appearance\n- **Labs** — In-progress features, off by default, opt-in, may change or be removed (currently hosting: Desktop Pet)\n- **Conversation Sharing** — Export any conversation to JSON in one click; API keys and local paths are auto-redacted before sharing\n- **29 Built-in Skills** — PDF/PPTX/DOCX/Excel generation, frontend design, canvas design, algorithmic art, Mermaid/SVG/infographics, Abu's built-in browser, optional Chrome bridge, deep research, Agent self-reflection (reflect), workflow automation, and more — one-click install, fully customizable\n- **MCP Protocol** — Connect to databases, search engines, GitHub, and other external services via Model Context Protocol\n- **Browser Automation** — Zero-setup built-in browser for ordinary web tasks, plus an optional Chrome extension bridge for existing tabs and signed-in sessions\n- **Computer Use** — Screenshot + mouse/keyboard control for desktop-level tasks, with sensitive app blocking, dangerous key interception, and a 5-minute session timeout\n- **HTTP Fetch** — Built-in safety gateway: URL length cap, embedded credential blocking, cloud metadata endpoint blocking, 10 MB download limit, 60-second timeout — no more raw `curl` blind spots\n\n### AI Services & Models\n\n- **12+ Cloud Providers** — Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (Bailian), Doubao (Volcengine), Moonshot, Zhipu GLM, MiniMax, SiliconFlow, Qiniu, OpenRouter, and more\n- **Local Models** — Zero-config Ollama integration with automatic local model discovery\n- **Custom Endpoints** — Connect any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible API\n- **Provider Management** — Add, edit, delete, reorder providers with connection health checks and latency detection\n- **Model Selector** — Switch models on-the-fly during conversations with capability badges (vision, tool use, web search, thinking, image generation, long context)\n- **Favorites & History** — Star frequently used models, quickly switch between recent ones\n- **Image Generation** — Built-in DALL-E 2 / DALL-E 3 support, plus any custom image-generation endpoint\n\n### Web Search\n\n- **Multiple Search Engines** — Bing, Brave, Tavily, SearXNG (self-hosted, no API key needed)\n- **Independent Configuration** — Search engine settings decoupled from main AI service\n\n### Automation & Triggers\n\n- **Scheduled Tasks** — Cron-based scheduling (e.g., daily AI news digest at 9 AM); runs missed while the app was closed are replayed in time order on next launch\n- **Trigger System** — Multiple event sources to automatically invoke agents:\n  - **File Watcher** — Monitor file create/modify/delete events with glob patterns\n  - **HTTP Webhook** — Auto-generated POST endpoints for external callbacks\n  - **IM Messages** — Trigger tasks on specific incoming messages\n  - **Cron Schedule** — Periodic execution on a time-based plan\n- **Trigger Permission Model** — Four capability levels (read-only → safe tools → full access → custom whitelist) for fine-grained control\n\n### IM Channel Integration\n\nTurn Abu into your team bot — just @Abu in your chat:\n\n- **Supported Platforms** — D-Chat, Feishu (Lark), DingTalk, WeCom, Slack\n- **Session Management** — Auto-isolate conversations by user/group/thread, auto-archive on timeout, \"continue last\" recovery\n- **Security Controls** — User allowlist, workspace path restrictions, capability level enforcement\n- **Response Modes** — Mention-only or all-messages\n\n### Memory & Context\n\n- **Three-tier file-based memory (Memdir architecture)**:\n  - **Personal Memory** — `~/.abu/memory/` multi-file directory, applies across all projects, auto-organized by topic with `MEMORY.md` index injected into the prompt\n  - **Project Memory** — `~/.abu/projects/<workspace>/memory/` auto-isolated per workspace, each entry is a separate `.md` file for easy reading, search, and pruning\n  - **Auto-migration** — Legacy `~/.abu/agents/abu/memory.md` and `{workspace}/.abu/MEMORY.md` are migrated automatically on startup\n- **Project Rules** (hand-written):\n  - `~/.abu/ABU.md` — User-level rules (cross-project)\n  - `{workspace}/.abu/ABU.md` — Project-level rules\n  - `{workspace}/.abu/rules/*.md` — Modular rules (loaded alphabetically, max 20 files)\n- **Project Aggregation** — Promote a workspace into a Project to aggregate its conversations; older conversations auto-backfilled with `projectId` on startup. Each project can independently configure default model, skill set, and MCP connectors\n- **Session Memory** — Large tool outputs automatically persisted to disk; compact summaries kept in-context to prevent context explosion\n- **Persistent Todos** — Per-conversation `todo_write` plans persisted to disk and survive app restarts\n- **Auto-Compaction** — Intelligently compresses long conversation history while preserving key context\n\n### Security & Privacy\n\n- **Three Permission Modes** — **Request Approval** (free read/write inside workspace; out-of-bounds writes and dangerous commands need confirmation; default) / **Smart Review** (out-of-bounds ops go to an AI reviewer: allow low-risk, block high-risk, ask only when unsure) / **Full Autonomy** (everything runs automatically except hard system red-lines); global default in Settings → Sandbox, also switchable per conversation via the chip above the composer\n- **Content Safety Scan** — Scans agent-authored skills / memory entries to catch dangerous instructions, prompt injection, hardware commands, and 120+ other risk patterns\n- **OS Sandbox (macOS only)** — macOS Seatbelt (`sandbox-exec`) confines a shell command's file access to the workspace. **Windows has no OS-enforced sandbox**: PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage restricts in-process language features, not file access, and a child `powershell.exe` does not inherit it. Treat Windows shell containment as advisory, not as a security boundary\n- **Network Isolation** — Local proxy + domain allowlist + private-network toggle. **Enforced through environment variables, not by the OS**: a command that bypasses the proxy (`curl --noproxy`, a runtime with its own proxy settings) still reaches the network. On Windows the toggle is not exposed in Settings and isolation is off by default\n- **Path & Command Safety** — Sensitive directories (system folders, SSH keys, etc.) blocked by default; dangerous commands (`rm -rf /`, etc.) caught statically\n- **Computer Use Safeguards** — Blocked sensitive apps (terminals, system settings, credential managers, IDEs), dangerous key interception (Cmd+Q, Cmd+Tab, Force Quit, Win+R), per-app grants you can revoke, confirmation before any consequential action, 5-minute timeout. These govern the Computer Use tool; **they do not constrain the shell tool**, which can reach the desktop by other means while no OS sandbox is in place\n- **Encrypted API Key Storage** — Windows DPAPI / macOS AES-256-GCM with a hardware-UUID-derived key; keys are no longer written to localStorage in plaintext\n- **Local-First** — Your data stays local, your API keys stay local — nothing goes through third-party servers\n- **Cross-Platform** — Supports macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) and Windows\n\n### Diagnostics & Troubleshooting\n\n- **One-Click Self-Check** — Settings → Diagnostic, runs through AI service connectivity, data & permissions, MCP, skills, network, app environment\n- **Diagnostic Bundle Export** — When something breaks, package logs / config / version info in one click (API keys and paths auto-redacted) and send it to the maintainer\n\n> For detailed feature documentation, see the [User Guide](docs/User-Guide.md)\n\n## Download\n\nHead to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/PM-Shawn/Abu-Cowork/releases) to download the latest version:\n\n| Platform | File |\n|----------|------|\n| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `Abu-x.x.x-mac-arm64.dmg` |\n| macOS (Intel) | `Abu-x.x.x-mac-x64.dmg` |\n| Windows x64 | `Abu-x.x.x-windows-x64-setup.exe` |\n\n> Official macOS packages are signed and notarized. The Windows installer is current-user only and does not need administrator rights, but remains Authenticode-unsigned; SmartScreen may require **More info → Run anyway**. See the [Installation Guide](docs/Installation-Guide.md).\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### 1. Configure AI Service\n\nOpen Abu → Settings → **AI Service Management**:\n\n- **Quickest setup**: Choose a provider (e.g., DeepSeek, Anthropic), enter your API Key, click verify\n- **Local models**: Install [Ollama](https://ollama.com) — Abu auto-discovers local models, no API key needed\n- **Custom endpoint**: Enter any OpenAI-compatible API's Base URL and Key\n\n### 2. Start Chatting\n\nReturn to the main screen, use the model selector to pick your preferred model, and start chatting.\n\n**Try these prompts:**\n\n```\nOrganize the files on my desktop by type\n```\n```\nExtract the tables from this PDF and generate an Excel file\n```\n```\nEvery morning at 9 AM, search for the latest AI news and generate a daily digest\n```\n```\nUse the frontend design skill to create a product landing page\n```\n```\nCreate a weekly report PPT for this week\n```\n\n### 3. Level Up\n\n- **Install skills**: Settings → Customize → Skill Store — install PDF, PPT, frontend design, and more\n- **Connect MCP**: Settings → MCP Connectors — one-click integration with GitHub, Playwright, etc.\n- **Set up schedules**: Have Abu automatically search news, run data, send reports daily\n- **Connect IM**: Settings → IM Channels — let your team @Abu directly in Lark/DingTalk\n\n> For more use cases, see the [User Guide](docs/User-Guide.md)\n\n## Built-in Skills (29 total)\n\n| Category | Skills |\n|----------|--------|\n| Document Generation | PDF, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX |\n| Design & Creative | Frontend Design, Canvas Design, Algorithmic Art, SVG Diagram, Mermaid Diagram, Infographic, Slack GIF Creator, HTML Widget |\n| Browser Automation | **Abu-Browser** (built-in, isolated session), **Abu-Chrome-Bridge** (optional Chrome extension for existing tabs and sign-in state) |\n| Developer Tools | Claude API, MCP Builder, Web Artifacts Builder, Webapp Testing (Playwright) |\n| Content Writing | Doc Co-authoring, Brand Guidelines, Internal Comms |\n| Automation | Schedule, Trigger, Alert SOP |\n| Project Management | Skill Creator, Project Init, Create Agent |\n| Agent Reflection | Reflect — lets the agent look back on a run and distill learnings |\n| Theming | Theme Factory (10+ preset themes applicable to any artifact) |\n\n> Beyond built-ins, Abu also supports **Self-Evolving Skills** — after multi-step complex flows, Abu proactively suggests \"crystallize this into a skill\" and grows a library tailored to your workflow. The action was\n      // allowed and ran (a human is here, and they may well be signing in);\n      // what changes is that the result now SAYS the session expired, so the\n      // model asks the user to sign in instead of retrying into the wall.\n      // Unattended never reaches this line — the gate refused above.\n      if (isBrowserTool && approval.browserExecution?.loginRequired && typeof result === 'string') {\n        result = `${result}\\n\\n${getI18n().commandConfirm.browserLoginRequiredHint}`;\n      }\n      await captureOutputs(result);\n      return result;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return unknownToolResult(name, toolContext);\n  } finally {\n    let completed = false;\n    try {\n      if (initialApproval) await releaseToolApproval(initialApproval);\n      assertOutputCurrent();\n      completed = true;\n      await outputCapture?.commit();\n    } finally {\n      outputPlanning?.dispose();\n      if (!completed) await outputCapture?.rollback();\n    }\n  }\n  } catch (error) {\n    if (error instanceof FileOperationDenied) return error.message;\n    throw error;\n  }\n}\n\n// ── OS Permission Error Detection ──\n// The detection + guide logic lives in the pure, store-free `osPermissionGuide`\n// module (re-exported here for existing importers) so the sidecar's local\n// path can share it without dragging registry.ts → chatStore — see that\n// module's doc. `FILE_TOOL_NAMES` there mirrors FILE_TOOL_PATH_MAP's keys; a\n// registry.test.ts case asserts the two stay in sync.\nexport { applyOSPermissionGuideIfNeeded, FILE_TOOL_NAMES } from './osPermissionGuide';\n\n// Re-export types for convenience\nexport type { ConfirmationInfo, DangerLevel };\n\n// ── HMR: re-register builtin tools when this module is hot-reloaded ──\nif (import.meta.hot) {\n  import.meta.hot.accept(() => {\n    // Module replaced — toolRegistry is now a fresh empty instance.\n    // Re-register builtins so tools don't disappear during development.\n    import('./builtins').then(({ registerBuiltinTools }) => {\n      registerBuiltinTools();\n      console.info('[HMR] Builtin tools re-registered');\n    });\n  });\n}\n"

      "path": "src/core/permissions/permissionMode.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Permission Mode System — controls tool execution confirmation behavior.\n *\n * Three tiers along a single autonomy axis (the workspace is the boundary):\n * - standard:   Inside the workspace, read/write/commands run freely. Escalations\n *               (writes to new directories, dangerous commands) require confirmation.\n * - smart:      Same boundary as standard, but escalations are routed to an AI\n *               reviewer instead of the user. (Reviewer lands in Phase 2; until then\n *               the gate degrades 'review' to 'confirm'.)\n * - autonomous: Everything runs automatically. Block-level commands, sensitive-path\n *               hard-blocks and the content guard still apply — they are enforced\n *               independently of the mode, not via these strategies.\n */\n\nimport type { ConfirmationInfo } from '../tools/registry';\nimport type { CmdBoundary } from './commandBoundary';\nimport computerUsePolicy from '../tools/computerUsePolicy.json';\n\n/** Permission mode determines how much autonomy the agent has before asking. */\nexport type PermissionMode = 'standard' | 'smart' | 'autonomous';\n\n/** Every permission mode, ordered along the autonomy axis. */\nexport const PERMISSION_MODES: readonly PermissionMode[] = ['standard', 'smart', 'autonomous'];\n\n/** Whether a value that did not come through the type system (a file on disk, an imported JSON) is a permission mode. */\nexport function isPermissionMode(value: unknown): value is PermissionMode {\n  return typeof value === 'string' && (PERMISSION_MODES as readonly string[]).includes(value);\n}\n\n/**\n * Outcome of a permission decision:\n * - allow:   proceed without asking\n * - confirm: ask the user\n * - review:  route to the AI reviewer (Phase 2); degrades to 'confirm' until wired\n */\nexport type PermissionDecision = 'allow' | 'confirm' | 'review';\nexport type ComputerUseAppRisk = 'ordinary' | 'approval-required';\nexport type ComputerUseAppDecision = 'allow' | 'confirm';\n\n/**\n * App identity is an independent Computer Use boundary inside the global\n * permission mode. High-consequence apps always require the user.\n */\nexport function decideComputerUseApp(\n  mode: PermissionMode,\n  risk: ComputerUseAppRisk,\n): ComputerUseAppDecision {\n  const safeMode: PermissionMode = mode === 'smart' || mode === 'autonomous'\n    ? mode\n    : 'standard';\n  return computerUsePolicy.modePolicy[safeMode][risk] as ComputerUseAppDecision;\n}\n\n/**\n * Strategy interface for permission decisions.\n * Each mode implements this to decide how a tool call is gated.\n */\nexport interface PermissionStrategy {\n  /**\n   * Decide gating for the run_command tool.\n   * @param boundary - whether the command writes outside the working dirs (best-effort)\n   */\n  decideCommand(info: ConfirmationInfo, readOnly: boolean, boundary?: CmdBoundary): PermissionDecision;\n\n  /** Decide gating for file tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, etc.). */\n  decideFileAccess(capability: 'read' | 'write', needsPermission: boolean): PermissionDecision;\n\n  /**\n   * Decide gating for MCP/other tools.\n   *\n   * @param consequence - 'state-changing' for actions that act on the user's\n   *   behalf inside a live session (browser click/fill/execute_js); 'read-only'\n   *   for observation. Omitted for tools with no consequence classification,\n   *   which stay ungated as before.\n   * @param alreadyGranted - the user already approved this class for the\n   *   current conversation, so the remaining actions of the task run freely\n   *   (same shape as Computer Use's per-task grant).\n   */\n  decideOtherTool(\n    consequence?: 'read-only' | 'state-changing',\n    alreadyGranted?: boolean,\n  ): PermissionDecision;\n}\n\n/**\n * Shared gate for consequence-classified non-command tools.\n * Mirrors `computerUsePolicy.modePolicy`'s `approval-required` row, which asks\n * in every mode — the browser is the same high-consequence surface whether it\n * is driven by Computer Use or by the automation tools.\n */\nfunction decideConsequentialTool(\n  consequence?: 'read-only' | 'state-changing',\n  alreadyGranted?: boolean,\n): PermissionDecision {\n  if (consequence !== 'state-changing') return 'allow';\n  return alreadyGranted ? 'allow' : 'confirm';\n}\n\n/** Whether a command's content classification counts as an escalation. */\nfunction isRiskyCommand(level: ConfirmationInfo['level']): boolean {\n  return level === 'danger' || level === 'warn';\n}\n\n/** standard: workspace-internal is free; escalations ask the user. Matches the old `default` behavior. */\nconst standardStrategy: PermissionStrategy = {\n  decideCommand(info, readOnly, boundary) {\n    if (readOnly) return 'allow';\n    if (isRiskyCommand(info.level)) return 'confirm';\n    // Safe content but writing outside the workspace → escalate.\n    if (boundary === 'outside') return 'confirm';\n    return 'allow';\n  },\n  decideFileAccess(_capability, needsPermission) {\n    // needsPermission === true means the path isn't in an authorized working dir yet.\n    return needsPermission ? 'confirm' : 'allow';\n  },\n  decideOtherTool(consequence, alreadyGranted) {\n    return decideConsequentialTool(consequence, alreadyGranted);\n  },\n};\n\n/** smart: same boundary as standard, but escalations go to the AI reviewer. */\nconst smartStrategy: PermissionStrategy = {\n  decideCommand(info, readOnly, boundary) {\n    if (readOnly) return 'allow';\n    return (isRiskyCommand(info.level) || boundary === 'outside') ? 'review' : 'allow';\n  },\n  decideFileAccess(_capability, needsPermission) {\n    return needsPermission ? 'review' : 'allow';\n  },\n  decideOtherTool(consequence, alreadyGranted) {\n    return decideConsequentialTool(consequence, alreadyGranted);\n  },\n};\n\n/** autonomous: everything proceeds. Block-level/sensitive-path/content-guard floors are enforced elsewhere. */\nconst autonomousStrategy: PermissionStrategy = {\n  decideCommand() {\n    return 'allow';\n  },\n  decideFileAccess() {\n    return 'allow';\n  },\n  // Even here the browser stays gated: `computerUsePolicy.modePolicy` keeps\n  // `approval-required` at 'confirm' in autonomous for exactly this surface.\n  decideOtherTool(consequence, alreadyGranted) {\n    return decideConsequentialTool(consequence, alreadyGranted);\n  },\n};\n\n/**\n * Get the permission strategy for a given mode. Unknown modes fall back to standard.\n */\nexport function getPermissionStrategy(mode: PermissionMode): PermissionStrategy {\n  switch (mode) {\n    case 'smart': return smartStrategy;\n    case 'autonomous': return autonomousStrategy;\n    case 'standard':\n    default: return standardStrategy;\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "src/core/tools/definitions/commandTools.ts",
      "content": "import type { CommandOutcome, ToolDefinition } from '../../../types';\nimport { getPlatform, getShell, isWindows } from '../../../utils/platform';\nimport { resolveCommandPython } from '../../../utils/pythonRuntime';\nimport { isSandboxEnabled, isNetworkIsolationEnabled } from '../../sandbox/config';\nimport { getWorkspaceReader } from '../../agent/ports/workspaceReader';\nimport { getAuthorizedPathsReader } from '../../agent/ports/authorizedPathsReader';\nimport { sandboxBlockClass } from '../../sandbox/blockClass';\nimport { showSandboxBlockedToast } from '../../sandbox/recovery';\nimport {\n  detectAppAutomationSandboxBlock,\n  getAppAutomationSandboxRecovery,\n  hasUnquotedShellControlSyntax,\n} from '../../sandbox/appAutomationRecovery';\nimport type { CommandOutput } from '../helpers/toolHelpers';\nimport { invokeTaskCommand, isTaskCommandAbortedError } from '../helpers/scopedCommand';\nimport { isReadOnlyCommand } from '../readOnlyDetector';\nimport { TOOL_NAMES } from '../toolNames';\nimport { format, getI18n } from '../../../i18n';\nimport { hasElectronCommandHost } from '../../../utils/electronHost';\nimport { COMMAND_OUTPUT_RULE, truncateText, type TruncationRule } from '../../context/truncation';\n\nconst PART_SEPARATOR = '\\n\\n';\nconst STDOUT_HEADING = 'stdout:\\n';\nconst STDERR_HEADING = 'stderr:\\n';\n\n/**\n * Cut each output stream on its own, so the joined result fits `rule` and the\n * recorded positions point into the text the model receives. When both\n * streams have text, stderr gets at most half of the budget and stdout the rest.\n */\nfunction boundCommandOutput(stdout: string, stderr: string, rule: TruncationRule): { stdout: string; stderr: string } {\n  if (stdout && stderr) {\n    const boundedStderr = truncateText(stderr, {\n      headLines: Math.floor(rule.headLines / 2),\n      tailLines: Math.floor(rule.tailLines / 2),\n      maxChars: Math.floor(rule.maxChars / 2),\n    });\n    return {\n      stdout: truncateText(stdout, { ...rule, maxChars: rule.maxChars - boundedStderr.length }),\n      stderr: boundedStderr,\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    stdout: stdout ? truncateText(stdout, rule) : '',\n    stderr: stderr ? truncateText(stderr, rule) : '',\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Global-workspace fallback for direct invocations that carry no context.\n * Sidecar-safe: the bare `getWorkspaceReader()` getter throws outside a\n * registered agent run (see `shims/workspaceReaderRun.ts`) — a throwing\n * fallback must degrade to \"no workspace\", never fail the command itself.\n */\nfunction safeGlobalWorkspacePath(): string | null {\n  try {\n    return getWorkspaceReader().getCurrentPath();\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction formatAppAutomationRecovery(\n  recovery: NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof getAppAutomationSandboxRecovery>>,\n): string {\n  const app = recovery.targetApp\n    ?? getI18n().sandbox.appAutomationTargetFallback;\n  return [\n    format(getI18n().sandbox.appAutomationToolError, { app }),\n  ].join('\\n\\n');\n}\n\nexport const runCommandTool: ToolDefinition = {\n  name: TOOL_NAMES.RUN_COMMAND,\n  get description() {\n    const plat = getPlatform();\n    const shell = getShell();\n    return `Execute a shell command on the user's computer (current platform: ${plat}, shell: ${shell}).\n\nImportant: prefer a dedicated tool when one is available:\n- Read a file → read_file\n- List a directory → list_directory\n- Search file contents → search_files\n- Find files → find_files\n- HTTP requests → http_fetch\n- Edit a file → edit_file\n\nThis tool is suitable for: moving/copying/renaming files (mv/cp), package management (npm/pip/brew), build and test (npm run/cargo build), Git operations, running Python scripts (automatically uses the built-in runtime). Set background=true for long-running services.`;\n  },\n  descriptionByFamily: {\n    get gpt() {\n      const plat = getPlatform();\n      const shell = getShell();\n      return `Execute a shell command on the user's computer (current platform: ${plat}, shell: ${shell}).\n\nPrefer a dedicated tool when one is offered:\n- Read a file → read_file\n- List a directory → list_directory\n- Search file contents → search_files\n- Find files → find_files\n- HTTP requests → http_fetch\n- Edit or create a file → apply_patch when it is offered, otherwise edit_file / write_file. Never write a file with cat, echo, printf, heredocs, shell redirection or a Python script.\n\nUse it for: moving/copying/renaming files (mv/cp), package management (npm/pip/brew), build and test (npm run/cargo build), Git operations, running Python scripts (the built-in runtime is used automatically). Set background=true for long-running services. Quote arguments carefully: backticks and $() in the command still execute.`;\n    },\n  },\n  inputSchema: {\n    type: 'object',\n    properties: {\n      command: { type: 'string', description: 'The shell command to execute' },\n      cwd: { type: 'string', description: 'Working directory for the command (optional, defaults to user home)' },\n      background: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Set to true for long-running services (servers, etc). Will start the process and return initial output after a few seconds.' },\n      timeout: { type: 'number', description: 'Timeout in seconds (default 30, max 300). Command will be killed if it exceeds this.' },\n    },\n    required: ['command'],\n  },\n  execute: async (input, context) => {\n    const command = input.command as string;\n    const cwd = input.cwd as string | undefined;\n    const background = input.background as boolean | undefined;\n    const timeout = input.timeout as number | undefined;\n    const abortSignal = context?.abortSignal;\n    if (abortSignal?.aborted) {\n      return 'Error executing command: command was aborted before it started';\n    }\n\n    try {\n      // Use embedded Python runtime if command starts with python/python3\n      const resolvedCommand = await resolveCommandPython(command);\n      if (abortSignal?.aborted) {\n        return 'Error executing command: command was aborted before it started';\n      }\n\n      // Exempt app-launcher commands from sandbox\n      // macOS: `open` uses LaunchServices via XPC, blocked by Seatbelt\n      // Windows: `start`/`Start-Process` exempted for consistency with ExecutionPolicy\n      const isLauncherCandidate = isWindows()\n        ? /^\\s*(start|Start-Process)\\s/i.test(resolvedCommand)\n        : /^\\s*open\\s/.test(resolvedCommand);\n      const isLauncherCmd = isLauncherCandidate\n        && (\n          !hasElectronCommandHost()\n          || !hasUnquotedShellControlSyntax(resolvedCommand)\n        );\n      const sandbox = isLauncherCmd ? false : isSandboxEnabled();\n\n      // Seatbelt does not contain the target app process: Apple Events can ask\n      // that app to mutate data outside the shell profile. Electron therefore\n      // blocks explicit cross-app AppleScript before spawn while Shell sandbox\n      // protection is enabled. Tauri stays unchanged during coexistence.\n      const preflightAppAutomationRecovery = sandbox && hasElectronCommandHost()\n        ? getAppAutomationSandboxRecovery(resolvedCommand)\n        : null;\n      if (preflightAppAutomationRecovery) {\n        context?.reportMetadata?.({\n          sandboxRecovery: preflightAppAutomationRecovery,\n        });\n        return formatAppAutomationRecovery(preflightAppAutomationRecovery);\n      }\n\n      // Use the shell/session-owned workspace from context. Scoped unattended\n      // runs fail closed when that trusted value is null/absent; only\n      // unscoped interactive/direct invocations may fall back to the global\n      // workspace reader.\n      // The fallback must not fail the command: in the sidecar the bare getter\n      // resolves an ambient-run mirror and THROWS outside a registered run —\n      // treat that as \"no workspace\" (cwd-less spawn), matching the shell's\n      // no-workspace behavior instead of erroring before the spawn.\n      const workspacePath = context?.authorizationScopeId !== undefined\n        ? (context.workspacePath ?? null)\n        : (context?.workspacePath ?? safeGlobalWorkspacePath());\n      const authorizedPaths = sandbox\n        ? await getAuthorizedPathsReader().getAuthorizedWritablePaths(context?.authorizationScopeId)\n        : [];\n      const extraWritablePaths = [\n        ...(context?.authorizationScopeId === undefined && workspacePath ? [workspacePath] : []),\n        ...authorizedPaths,\n      ];\n\n      // Use custom Tauri command defined in Rust\n      const output = await invokeTaskCommand<CommandOutput & { backgroundCommandId?: string; running?: boolean }>('run_shell_command', {\n        command: resolvedCommand,\n        cwd: cwd || workspacePath || null,\n        background: background || false,\n        timeout: Math.min(Math.max(1, timeout ?? 30), 300),\n        sandboxEnabled: sandbox,\n        networkIsolation: isNetworkIsolationEnabled(),\n        extraWritablePaths,\n      }, context, {\n        commandIdPrefix: 'run-command',\n        keepAbortListenerAfterResolve: (result) => background === true && result.code === 0,\n      });\n\n      const appAutomationRecovery = sandbox\n        ? detectAppAutomationSandboxBlock(resolvedCommand, output.stderr, output.code)\n        : null;\n      if (appAutomationRecovery) {\n        context?.reportMetadata?.({\n          sandboxRecovery: appAutomationRecovery,\n        });\n      }\n\n      // Only a blocked *write* gets the \"authorize this directory\" toast —\n      // an exec/read/network/unclassified block has no directory to authorize,\n      // so the toast would be misleading. Every class still reaches the model\n      // through the annotated stderr below. AppleScript cross-app blocks render\n      // a task-local recovery card instead.\n      if (!appAutomationRecovery && sandbox && sandboxBlockClass(output.stderr) === 'write') {\n        showSandboxBlockedToast(resolvedCommand);\n      }\n\n      const { stdout, stderr } = boundCommandOutput(\n        output.stdout.trim(),\n        output.stderr.trim(),\n        COMMAND_OUTPUT_RULE,\n      );\n      const commandOutcome: CommandOutcome = { exitCode: output.code };\n      const parts: string[] = [];\n      // Where the next part starts in the joined result.\n      const nextStart = (): number => (parts.length === 0 ? 0 : parts.join(PART_SEPARATOR).length + PART_SEPARATOR.length);\n      if (appAutomationRecovery) {\n        parts.push(formatAppAutomationRecovery(appAutomationRecovery));\n      }\n      if (stdout) {\n        const start = nextStart() + STDOUT_HEADING.length;\n        parts.push(`${STDOUT_HEADING}${stdout}`);\n        commandOutcome.stdout = [start, start + stdout.length];\n      }\n      if (stderr) {\n        const start = nextStart() + STDERR_HEADING.length;\n        parts.push(`${STDERR_HEADING}${stderr}`);\n        commandOutcome.stderr = [start, start + stderr.length];\n      }\n      parts.push(`exit code: ${output.code}`);\n      if (output.backgroundCommandId && output.running === true) {\n        commandOutcome.background = true;\n        parts.push(`Background command id: ${output.backgroundCommandId} (still running). Use background_command_output to read later output, stop_background_command to stop it.`);\n      }\n\n      context?.reportMetadata?.({ commandOutcome });\n      return parts.join(PART_SEPARATOR);\n    } catch (err) {\n      if (isTaskCommandAbortedError(err)) {\n        return 'Error executing command: command was aborted before it started';\n      }\n      return `Error executing command: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`;\n    }\n  },\n  isConcurrencySafe: (input) => isReadOnlyCommand(String(input.command ?? '')),\n};\n"
    },

      "path": "src/core/sandbox/config.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Sandbox configuration — determines whether OS-level sandboxing is enabled.\n * On macOS, uses Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) to restrict shell command file access.\n * On Windows, uses PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode + ExecutionPolicy Restricted.\n * On other platforms, returns false (no OS-level sandbox available).\n */\n\nimport { isMacOS, isWindows } from '@/utils/platform';\nimport { getSettingsReader } from '@/core/agent/ports/settingsReader';\nimport { invoke } from '@tauri-apps/api/core';\n\n/**\n * Whether this platform has an OS-level sandbox backend at all.\n * Single source of truth for platform capability — the settings UI\n * (SandboxSection) must gate on this, not re-derive its own platform\n * list, so adding a platform here can't silently drift from the UI.\n */\nexport function isOsSandboxCapable(): boolean {\n  return isMacOS() || isWindows();\n}\n\n/** Whether OS-level sandbox should be enabled for shell commands */\nexport function isSandboxEnabled(): boolean {\n  if (!isOsSandboxCapable()) return false;\n  return getSettingsReader().getSnapshot().sandboxEnabled;\n}\n\n/** Whether network isolation (proxy-based domain whitelist) is enabled */\nexport function isNetworkIsolationEnabled(): boolean {\n  if (!isOsSandboxCapable()) return false;\n  const state = getSettingsReader().getSnapshot();\n  return state.sandboxEnabled && state.networkIsolationEnabled;\n}\n\nlet proxyStarted = false;\n\n/** Start the network proxy if network isolation is enabled. Call once at app init. */\nexport async function initNetworkProxy(): Promise<void> {\n  if (proxyStarted || !isOsSandboxCapable()) return;\n\n  const state = getSettingsReader().getSnapshot();\n  if (!state.networkIsolationEnabled) return;\n\n  try {\n    const port = await invoke<number>('start_network_proxy', {\n      whitelist: state.networkWhitelist,\n      allowPrivateNetworks: state.allowPrivateNetworks,\n    });\n    proxyStarted = true;\n    console.log(`[sandbox] Network proxy started on port ${port}`);\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('[sandbox] Failed to start network proxy:', err);\n  }\n}\n\n/** Sync whitelist changes to the running proxy. */\nexport async function syncNetworkWhitelist(): Promise<void> {\n  if (!proxyStarted) return;\n  const state = getSettingsReader().getSnapshot();\n  try {\n    await invoke('update_network_whitelist', {\n      whitelist: state.networkWhitelist,\n      allowPrivateNetworks: state.allowPrivateNetworks,\n    });\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('[sandbox] Failed to update whitelist:', err);\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "electron/commandHost.cjs",
      "content": "/**\n * Electron main-side command-execution host — port of the Tauri\n * `run_shell_command` / `run_argv_command` / `get_env_vars` commands\n * (src-tauri/src/lib.rs) PLUS the macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) integration\n * that wraps every sandboxed invocation (src-tauri/src/sandbox.rs).\n *\n * These three commands are the agent's core command-execution path — used by\n * ~15 frontend call sites (commandTools.ts, fileTools.ts, toolHelpers.ts,\n * skill/preprocessor.ts, mcp/client.ts, computerTools.ts). The Tauri version\n * wraps EVERY command in a macOS seatbelt sandbox via `sandbox-exec` (a macOS\n * SYSTEM binary — no native dep needed) unless the caller explicitly passes\n * `sandboxEnabled: false`. A naive child_process port would silently run\n * agent commands UNCONFINED — this file exists specifically to not do that.\n *\n * Argument-name contract (verified against actual frontend call sites, not\n * the Rust parameter names): Tauri's `invoke()` auto-converts camelCase JS\n * keys to the snake_case Rust parameter names (e.g. `allowPrivateNetworks` ->\n * `allow_private_networks`); Electron's raw IPC does no such conversion. So\n * this dispatcher reads the CAMELCASE keys the frontend actually sends\n * (`sandboxEnabled`, `extraWritablePaths`, `networkIsolation`) — matching,\n * byte for byte, what reaches the Rust side today. Two call sites\n * (skill/preprocessor.ts, skill/skillHooks.ts) pass `sandbox`/\n * `extra_writable_paths` (wrong casing / not a real param name) — those keys\n * don't match on the Tauri side either (silently ignored, falling back to\n * defaults), so reading only the camelCase names here reproduces the exact\n * same (accidental) behavior rather than \"fixing\" a pre-existing quirk.\n *\n * Wired from electron/tauriHost.cjs via commandDispatch(app, cmd, args) —\n * see the wiring comment there for the dispatch-order slot.\n */\n'use strict';\n\nconst os = require('node:os');\nconst fs = require('node:fs');\nconst path = require('node:path');\nconst { spawn, spawnSync, execFileSync } = require('node:child_process');\nconst { ownedChildProcesses } = require('./ownedChildProcesses.cjs');\nconst { resourceRoot, REPO_ROOT } = require('./appEnv.cjs');\nconst {\n  resolveBundledProgram,\n  runtimeLayout,\n  withBundledRuntimeEnv,\n} = require('./runtimeResolver.cjs');\nconst { runtimeState } = require('./runtimeObservability.cjs');\n\n// ── Seatbelt (SBPL) profile generation — line-for-line port of\n// src-tauri/src/sandbox.rs's generate_seatbelt_profile() ──\n\n/**\n * Sensitive paths under $HOME that should never be readable.\n * Maintained independently from TS pathSafety.ts (defense in depth).\n * IDENTICAL to sandbox.rs's SENSITIVE_READ_PATHS — do not let these drift.\n */\nconst SENSITIVE_READ_PATHS = [\n  '.ssh',\n  '.gnupg',\n  '.gpg',\n  '.aws/credentials',\n  '.azure',\n  '.config/gcloud',\n  '.env',\n  '.env.local',\n  '.env.production',\n  '.npmrc',\n  '.pypirc',\n  '.netrc',\n  '.docker/config.json',\n  '.kube/config',\n  '.git-credentials',\n  '.password-store',\n See\n * docs/2026-07-22-phase2-sliceC-secret-migration-plan.md for that deferred\n * migration.\n */\n'use strict';\n\nconst path = require('node:path');\nconst fs = require('node:fs');\nconst { safeStorage } = require('electron');\nconst { abuAppDataDir } = require('./appEnv.cjs');\nconst { secretStoreFileName } = require('./devShellIdentity.cjs');\n\n/** @type {string | null} */\nlet filePath = null;\n/** key -> base64(encryptString(value)) */\nlet store = new Map();\n/** Keys present on disk that failed to decrypt (load-time or subsequent). */\nlet failedKeys = new Set();\nlet encryptionAvailable = false;\nlet initialized = false;\n\nfunction warn(msg, extra) {\n  console.warn(`[secretStore] ${msg}`, extra !== undefined ? extra : '');\n}\n\nfunction errMsg(err) {\n  return err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);\n}\n\n/** Read the on-disk JSON blob into `store`. Decrypt is LAZY (see note). */\nfunction loadFromDisk() {\n  store = new Map();\n  failedKeys = new Set();\n  if (!filePath || !fs.existsSync(filePath)) return;\n\n  let raw;\n  try {\n    raw = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');\n  } catch (err) {\n    warn('failed to read secrets file, starting empty store', errMsg(err));\n    return;\n  }\n  if (raw.trim().length === 0) return;\n\n  try {\n    const json = JSON.parse(raw);\n    for (const [key, b64] of Object.entries(json)) {\n      if (typeof b64 === 'string') store.set(key, b64);\n    }\n  } catch (err) {\n    // Corrupt/unparseable file: do NOT start empty and let the next write\n    // overwrite it — that would permanently discard recoverable ciphertext\n    // (silent total key loss). Preserve the file aside first, THEN continue\n    // empty so a fresh store can be built without destroying the old blobs.\n    const aside = `${filePath}.corrupt-${Date.now()}`;\n    try {\n      fs.renameSync(filePath, aside);\n      warn(`secrets file corrupt/unparseable — preserved as ${aside}, starting empty`, errMsg(err));\n    } catch (renameErr) {\n      warn('secrets file corrupt AND could not be preserved aside', errMsg(renameErr));\n    }\n    store = new Map();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  // failedKeys is populated LAZILY by get() — the frontend reads every provider\n  // key at boot, so a failed decrypt is caught there. We deliberately do NOT\n  // eager-decrypt every entry here: that would run a synchronous decryptString\n  // over the whole store on the main thread before the window, and on a\n  // re-signed macOS build (dev rebuilds ad-hoc re-sign) the first Keychain\n  // access can raise a modal prompt that hangs launch. When safeStorage is\n  // unavailable we can't read anything at all, so mark all as failed up front\n  // (no decrypt call involved).\n  if (!encryptionAvailable) {\n    for (const key of store.keys()) failedKeys.add(key);\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Atomic durable write: temp file + fsync + rename. THROWS on failure so the\n * caller (secret_set/delete/clear_all) rejects the invoke — a swallowed write\n * error would report a save as successful yet be gone after restart (matches\n * the Tauri backend, whose persist() propagates its Err to the frontend).\n */\nfunction persist() {\n  if (!filePath) return;\n  const obj = {};\n  for (const [k, v] of store) obj[k] = v;\n  const json = JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2);\n  const tmp = `${filePath}.tmp`;\n  fs.writeFileSync(tmp, json, 'utf8');\n  // fsync the temp file's data blocks before the rename (Rust's sync_all), so a\n  // crash/power-loss right after the (journaled) rename can't expose a\n  // truncated/zero-length store — which would silently lose every key.\n  const fd = fs.openSync(tmp, 'r+');\n  try {\n    fs.fsyncSync(fd);\n  } finally {\n    fs.closeSync(fd);\n  }\n  fs.renameSync(tmp, filePath);\n}\n\n/**\n * Called once from registerTauriHost(app), i.e. after app 'ready' (safeStorage\n * requires the app to be ready on some platforms).\n * @param {import('electron').App} app\n */\nfunction initSecretStore(app) {\n  if (initialized) return;\n  initialized = true;\n\n  const dir = abuAppDataDir(app);\n  try {\n    fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });\n  } catch {\n    /* best-effort; write path below will surface a real error if this failed */\n  }\n  filePath = path.join(dir, secretStoreFileName({ isPackaged: app.isPackaged }));\n\n  try {\n    encryptionAvailable = safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() && safeStorage.getSelectedStorageBackend?.() !== 'basic_text';\n  } catch (err) {\n    encryptionAvailable = false;\n    warn('safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() threw', errMsg(err));\n  }\n\n  if (!encryptionAvailable) {\n    warn(\n      'safeStorage encryption is NOT available on this system — operating in degraded mode: ' +\n        'secret_get returns null, secret_set throws (surfaced to the renderer) rather than ' +\n        'silently storing plaintext.'\n    );\n  }\n\n  loadFromDisk();\n\n  if (failedKeys.size > 0) {\n    warn(\n      `${failedKeys.size} entrie(s) failed to decrypt at load (hardware/OS-key change likely):`,\n      [...failedKeys]\n    );\n  }\n}\n\n/** @param {string} key */\nfunction get(key) {\n  if (!encryptionAvailable) return null;\n  const b64 = store.get(key);\n  if (b64 === undefined) return null;\n  try {\n    const plain = safeStorage.decryptString(Buffer.from(b64, 'base64'));\n    failedKeys.delete(key);\n    return plain;\n  } catch (err) {\n    failedKeys.add(key);\n    warn(`decrypt failed for key \"${key}\"`, errMsg(err));\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * @param {string} key\n * @param {string} value\n */\nfunction set(key, value) {\n  if (!encryptionAvailable) {\n    // A write silently dropped would look like a successful save (the key just\n    // \"didn't stick\"). Surface it to the renderer instead.\n    const msg = 'safeStorage encryption unavailable — cannot store secret securely';\n    warn(msg);\n    throw new Error(msg);\n  }\n  // No swallowing catch: an encrypt or persist (durability) failure must reject\n  // secret_set so the user learns the key wasn't saved, rather than seeing a\n  // fake success and finding it gone after restart (matches the Tauri backend).\n  const buf = safeStorage.encryptString(String(value));\n  store.set(key, buf.toString('base64'));\n  failedKeys.delete(key);\n  persist();\n}\n\n/** @param {string} key */\nfunction del(key) {\n  store.delete(key);\n  failedKeys.delete(key);\n  persist();\n}\n\n/** @param {string} key */\nfunction has(key) {\n  // Exclude undecryptable keys — matches Tauri macOS, where the in-memory index\n  // holds only decryptable secrets (failed keys live only in failed_keys()).\n  return store.has(key) && !failedKeys.has(key);\n}\n\nfunction list() {\n  return [...store.keys()].filter((k) => !failedKeys.has(k));\n}\n\nfunction getFailedKeys() {\n  return [...failedKeys];\n}\n\n/** Wipe everything. `knownKeys` is accepted (contract parity) but ignored — mirrors macOS Tauri behavior. */\nfunction clearAll() {\n  store.clear();\n  failedKeys.clear();\n  persist();\n}\n\nconst SECRET_CMDS = new Set([\n  'secret_get',\n  'secret_set',\n  'secret_delete',\n  'secret_has',\n  'secret_list',\n  'secret_failed_keys',\n  'secret_clear_all',\n]);\n\n/**\n * Map a `secret_*` command to the store. Returns `undefined` when `cmd` is\n * not one of the 7 secret commands, so tauriHost.cjs knows to fall through\n * to its own dispatch()/default stub.\n * @param {string} cmd\n * @param {Record<string, unknown>} [args]\n */\nfunction secretDispatch(cmd, args) {\n  if (!SECRET_CMDS.has(cmd)) return undefined;\n  const a = args || {};\n  switch (cmd) {\n    case 'secret_get':\n      return get(String(a.key));\n    case 'secret_set':\n      set(String(a.key), String(a.value));\n      return null;\n    case 'secret_delete':\n      del(String(a.key));\n      return null;\n    case 'secret_has':\n      return has(String(a.key));\n    case 'secret_list':\n      return list();\n    case 'secret_failed_keys':\n      return getFailedKeys();\n    case 'secret_clear_all':\n      clearAll();\n      return null;\n    default:\n      return undefined;\n  }\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { initSecretStore, secretDispatch };\n"

      "content": "import type { LLMAdapter, ChatOptions, ToolChoice } from './adapter';\nimport { LLMError, classifyError, LOG_TOOL_ARG_PREVIEW, buildToolParseError } from './adapter';\nimport type { Message, StreamEvent, ToolDefinition } from '../../types';\nimport { getTauriFetch } from './tauriFetch';\nimport { normalizeMessages } from './messageNormalizer';\nimport type { PreparedTurn, PreparedContentBlock } from './messageNormalizer';\nimport {\n  createHeartbeat,\n  anySignal,\n  localFirstResponseTimeoutError,\n  DEFAULT_STREAM_HANG_TIMEOUT_MS as STREAM_HANG_TIMEOUT_MS,\n  LOCAL_FIRST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS,\n} from './heartbeat';\nimport { createLogger } from '../logging/logger';\nimport { buildFullChatUrl } from './urlUtils';\nimport { applyModelRequestProcessors } from './modelRequestProcessors';\nimport { resolveModelProfile } from './modelProfile';\nimport { rejectedCapabilities } from './rejectionMemory';\nimport type { ReasoningReplay } from './model-data/families';\nimport { observeCompatEvent } from '../observability/compatEvents';\nimport { createDefaultUsageRecorder, type UsageAttemptRecorder } from './usageRecorder';\nimport { createTextToolCallParser, type TextSegment, type TextToolCall } from './textToolCalls';\n\nconst logger = createLogger('openai-compatible');\n\n// ── Hang-ceiling timeout helper (code-review fix #10) ──\n//\n// chat() arms this same pattern at two phases of a request that can each\n// hang unbounded if the server accepts the connection but never responds:\n// the initial connect/header wait and the max_tokens-retry connect/header wait.\n// Consolidated here so the timeout semantics (retryable, retryAfterMs) live\n// in one place; only the per-phase message wording still varies by call site.\n\n/**\n * Arm a hang-ceiling timer: aborts `streamAbort` after `timeoutMs` (the shared\n * 180s ceiling unless a caller passes another) and flips a flag the caller's\n * catch block can check to distinguish \"timed out\" from any other\n * abort/connection failure. Returns `timedOut()` (a function, since the flag\n * flips asynchronously after `armHangTimer` returns) and `clear()` to cancel\n * the timer once the awaited operation settles.\n */\nfunction armHangTimer(\n  streamAbort: AbortController,\n  timeoutMs: number = STREAM_HANG_TIMEOUT_MS,\n): { timedOut: () => boolean; clear: () => void } {\n  let timedOut = false;\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => {\n    timedOut = true;\n    streamAbort.abort();\n  }, timeoutMs);\n  return {\n    timedOut: () => timedOut,\n    clear: () => clearTimeout(timer),\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the LLMError thrown when a hang-ceiling timer (see `armHangTimer`)\n * fired before the awaited operation settled. `prefix`/`suffix` carry the\n * per-site phase wording — e.g. `hangTimeoutError('连接超时', '未收到服务器响应头')`\n * reproduces the connect-phase message exactly; `retryable`/`retryAfterMs`\n * are identical across both call sites.\n */\nfunction hangTimeoutError(prefix: string, suffix: string): LLMError {\n  return new LLMError(`${prefix}：${STREAM_HANG_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000} 秒${suffix}`, 'network_error', {\n    retryable: true,\n    retryAfterMs: 2000,\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Normalise a provider's `usage` response object into Abu's TokenUsage\n * shape, including prompt-caching fields. Each vendor uses a different\n * field name for cache hits, so we probe all known shapes:\n *\n *  - OpenAI standard: `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`\n *    (also豆包/火山引擎, 阿里百炼, 智谱 GLM when they follow the spec)\n *  - DeepSeek custom: `usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens` (+ `_miss_tokens`)\n *  - Some legacy paths put `cached_tokens` at the top level\n *\n * Anthropic's cache_creation_input_tokens has no OpenAI equivalent\n * (their auto-caching doesn't charge for writes), so we leave that\n * field undefined here.\n */\nfunction extractUsage(usage: Record<string, unknown>): {\n  inputTokens: number;\n  outputTokens: number;\n  cacheReadInputTokens?: number;\n} {\n  const inputTokens = (usage.prompt_tokens as number) ?? 0;\n  const outputTokens = (usage.completion_tokens as number) ?? 0;\n\n  let cacheReadInputTokens: number | undefined;\n  const details = usage.prompt_tokens_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;\n  if (details && typeof details.cached_tokens === 'number') {\n    cacheReadInputTokens = details.cached_tokens;\n  } else if (typeof usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens === 'number') {\n    // DeepSeek\n    cacheReadInputTokens = usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens;\n  } else if (typeof usage.cached_tokens === 'number') {\n    // Some providers flatten the field to the top level\n    cacheReadInputTokens = usage.cached_tokens;\n  }\n\n  return { inputTokens, outputTokens, ...(cacheReadInputTokens !== undefined ? { cacheReadInputTokens } : {}) };\n}\n\n/**\n * If the error body indicates that `max_tokens` exceeds the model's limit,\n * return the actual supported limit. Returns null otherwise.\n * Handles: \"max_tokens is too large: 32768. This model supports at most 4096 completion tokens\"\n */\nfunction extractMaxTokensLimit(errorBody: string): number | null {\n  try {\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(errorBody) as { error?: { message?: string; param?: string } };\n    if (parsed.error?.param === 'max_tokens' && parsed.error.message) {\n      const m = /supports at most (\\d+)/i.exec(parsed.error.message);\n      if (m) return parseInt(m[1], 10);\n    }\n  } catch { /* not JSON */ }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Safely parse a tool-call arguments string into a Record.\n * - Empty string → {} (let validateToolInput surface missing required fields)\n * - Non-object parse results (null, array, primitive) → {} (defensive)\n * - Parse failure → null (caller should mark _parse_error)\n */\nfunction safeParseToolArgs(args: string): Record<string, unknown> | null {\n  if (!args || !args.trim()) return {};\n  try {\n    const v = JSON.parse(args);\n    if (v && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v)) {\n      return v as Record<string, unknown>;\n    }\n    return {};\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the input object for a tool_use event from a streamed tool call buffer.\n * Logs full diagnostic context on parse failure so future issues can be traced\n * from disk logs (appDataDir/logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log).\n */\nfunction buildToolInput(\n  tc: { id: string; name: string; args: string },\n  source: string,\n): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const parsed = safeParseToolArgs(tc.args);\n  if (parsed !== null) return parsed;\n  return buildToolParseError(tc.args, { source, tool: tc.name }, logger);\n}\n\n/**\n * Flush only the buffered tool calls whose arguments parse successfully, dropping\n * malformed/partial ones. Mirrors the finish_reason='length' invariant: never hand\n * a broken tool call to the agent loop (which would surface a spurious `_parse_error`\n * tool execution instead of a clean turn). Use this on the abnormal terminal\n * branches (error / content_filter / refusal / unknown finish_reason) where there is\n * no max_tokens escalation path to recover a truncated call. Returns true if any\n * tool_use was emitted.\n */\nfunction emitParseableToolCalls(\n  toolCallBuffers: Map<number, { id: string; name: string; args: string }>,\n  onEvent: (event: StreamEvent) => void,\n): boolean {\n  let emitted = false;\n  for (const [, tc] of toolCallBuffers) {\n    const parsed = safeParseToolArgs(tc.args);\n    if (parsed === null) continue; // drop malformed — do not emit a _parse_error tool call\n    onEvent({ type: 'tool_use', id: tc.id, name: tc.name, input: parsed });\n    emitted = true;\n  }\n  return emitted;\n}\n\n// OpenAI multimodal content part\ntype OpenAIContentPart =\n  | { type: 'text'; text: string }\n  | { type: 'image_url'; image_url: { url: string } };\n\ninterface OpenAIMessage {\n  role: 'system' | 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool';\n  content: string | OpenAIContentPart[] | null;\n  tool_calls?: { id: string; type: 'function'; function: { name: string; arguments: string } }[];\n  tool_call_id?: string;\n  // DeepSeek R1 requires reasoning_content on assistant messages in multi-turn\n  reasoning_content?: string | null;\n}\n\nfunction convertTools(tools: ToolDefinition[]) {\n  return tools.map((t) => ({\n    type: 'function' as const,\n    function: {\n      name: t.name,\n      description: t.description,\n      parameters: t.inputSchema,\n    },\n  }));\n}\n\n// OpenAI-compatible chat has no document/file content type, so PDF attachments\n// can't be sent. Leave a text breadcrumb instead of dropping them silently —\n// otherwise the model sees nothing and may claim no file was provided.\n// LLM-facing → English.\nexport const DOCUMENT_UNSUPPORTED_NOTE =\n  '[A document was attached but the current model cannot receive file attachments. ' +\n  'Tell the user their model does not support documents, or ask them to paste the relevant text.]';\n\n/** 工具结果里的截图随后作为一条用户消息补发时附带的说明（给模型看，英文）。 */\nexport const TOOL_RESULT_IMAGES_NOTE =\n  '[SCREENSHOT] Tool results produced these screenshot(s). You MUST describe what you actually see in the image before deciding next action. If you cannot see the image, say \"I cannot see the screenshot\" — do NOT guess or fabricate what is on screen.';\n\n/** Convert PreparedContentBlock[] to OpenAI content parts */\nfunction toOpenAIContentParts(blocks: PreparedContentBlock[]): OpenAIContentPart[] {\n  const parts: OpenAIContentPart[] = [];\n  for (const b of blocks) {\n    if (b.type === 'text') {\n      parts.push({ type: 'text', text: b.text });\n    } else if (b.type === 'image') {\n      parts.push({\n        type: 'image_url',\n        image_url: { url: `data:${b.mediaType};base64,${b.data}` },\n      });\n    } else if (b.type === 'document') {\n      // OpenAI format has no document part — leave a breadcrumb (see note above).\n      parts.push({ type: 'text', text: DOCUMENT_UNSUPPORTED_NOTE });\n    }\n  }\n  return parts;\n}\n\n/**\n * Serialize PreparedTurn[] into OpenAI-compatible messages.\n *\n * Thin serializer — all logic (orphan fix, ID gen, image extraction) is in normalizeMessages.\n */\nfunction serializeForOpenAI(\n  turns: PreparedTurn[],\n  systemPrompt: string | undefined,\n  reasoningReplay: ReasoningReplay,\n): OpenAIMessage[] {\n  const result: OpenAIMessage[] = [];\n\n  if (systemPrompt) {\n    result.push({ role: 'system', content: systemPrompt });\n  }\n\n  for (const turn of turns) {\n    if (turn.kind === 'user') {\n      const hasImages = turn.content.some((b) => b.type === 'image');\n      if (hasImages) {\n        const parts = toOpenAIContentParts(turn.content);\n        // Some providers require at least one text part alongside images\n        if (!parts.some((p) => p.type === 'text')) {\n          parts.unshift({ type: 'text', text: ' ' });\n        }\n        result.push({ role: 'user', content: parts });\n      } else {\n        const text = turn.content\n          .map((b) => (b.type === 'text' ? b.text : b.type === 'document' ? DOCUMENT_UNSUPPORTED_NOTE : ''))\n          .join('');\n        result.push({ role: 'user', content: text });\n      }\n    } else {\n      // Assistant turn\n      if (turn.toolCalls.length > 0) {\n        // Build OpenAI tool_calls array\n        const toolCalls = turn.toolCalls.map((tc) => ({\n          id: tc.id,\n          type: 'function' as const,\n          function: {\n            name: tc.name,\n            arguments: JSON.stringify(tc.input),\n          },\n        }));\n\n        const assistantMsg: OpenAIMessage = {\n          role: 'assistant',\n          content: turn.text || null,\n          tool_calls: toolCalls,\n        };\n        if (turn.thinking && reasoningReplay !== 'none') {\n          assistantMsg.reasoning_content = turn.thinking;\n        } else if (reasoningReplay === 'reasoning_content-or-empty') {\n          // Kimi K2.5 / DeepSeek R1 in thinking mode require reasoning_content\n          // on every assistant message carrying tool_calls. Fill empty string\n          // when the turn has no captured thinking.\n          assistantMsg.reasoning_content = '';\n        }\n        result.push(assistantMsg);\n\n        // Add tool results — normalizeMessages guarantees every tool_use has a result\n        // OpenAI only supports images in role:\"user\", not in role:\"tool\"\n        const pendingImages: OpenAIContentPart[] = [];\n        for (const tc of turn.toolCalls) {\n          result.push({\n            role: 'tool',\n            tool_call_id: tc.id,\n            content: tc.result,\n          });\n          // Collect images for a follow-up user message\n          for (const img of tc.resultImages) {\n            pendingImages.push({\n              type: 'image_url',\n              image_url: { url: `data:${img.mediaType};base64,${img.data}` },\n            });\n          }\n        }\n        // Inject collected images as a user message so the model can actually see them\n        if (pendingImages.length > 0) {\n          result.push({\n            role: 'user',\n            content: [\n              { type: 'text' as const, text: TOOL_RESULT_IMAGES_NOTE },\n              ...pendingImages,\n            ],\n          });\n        }\n      } else {\n        const assistantMsg: OpenAIMessage = { role: 'assistant', content: turn.text };\n        if (turn.thinking && reasoningReplay !== 'none') {\n          assistantMsg.reasoning_content = turn.thinking;\n        }\n        result.push(assistantMsg);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  return result;\n}\n\n/** Convert messages through normalize → serialize pipeline */\nfunction convertMessages(\n  messages: Message[],\n  systemPrompt: string | undefined,\n  supportsVision: boolean | undefined,\n  reasoningReplay: ReasoningReplay,\n): OpenAIMessage[] {\n  const turns = normalizeMessages(messages, { supportsVision: supportsVision !== false });\n  return serializeForOpenAI(turns, systemPrompt, reasoningReplay);\n}\n\n/**\n * Convert Abu's ToolChoice into an OpenAI-compatible tool_choice value.\n *\n * Mapping:\n *   undefined              → undefined  (omit field — preserves current default behaviour)\n *   { type: 'auto' }      → 'auto'\n *   { type: 'any' }       → 'required'\n *   { type: 'tool', name} → { type: 'function', function: { name } }\n */\nexport function toOpenAIToolChoice(\n  tc: ToolChoice | undefined,\n): 'auto' | 'required' | { type: 'function'; function: { name: string } } | undefined {\n  if (tc === undefined) return undefined;\n  if (tc.type === 'auto') return 'auto';\n  if (tc.type === 'any') return 'required';\n  return { type: 'function', function: { name: tc.name } };\n}\n\nexport class OpenAICompatibleAdapter implements LLMAdapter {\n  async chat(\n    messages: Message[],\n    options: ChatOptions,\n    emitEvent: (event: StreamEvent) => void\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    // 用量采集在 provider 边界。这个适配器有二十多处结束事件的发出点，结清统一挂在\n    // The text of an\n   * image-only result is a fixed placeholder, so without these two different\n   * screenshots would look like the same observation.\n   */\n  images: string[];\n  error: boolean;\n}\n\n/** Maximum history needed by the deterministic M0 semantic loop checks. */\nexport const SEMANTIC_TOOL_LOOP_WINDOW = 6;\n\nconst META_TOOL_NAMES = new Set([\n  'tool_search',\n  'use_skill',\n  'read_skill_file',\n  'read_me',\n  'skill_view',\n  'recall',\n  'read_memory',\n]);\n\nfunction stableValue(value: unknown): unknown {\n  if (typeof value === 'string') return value.trim().replace(/\\s+/g, ' ');\n  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(stableValue);\n  if (value && typeof value === 'object') {\n    const source = value as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return Object.fromEntries(\n      Object.keys(source).sort().map(key => [key, stableValue(source[key])]),\n    );\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n\n/** Small deterministic hash; keeps tool inputs/results out of retained guard state. */\nfunction hashText(value: string): string {\n  let hash = 0x811c9dc5;\n  for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i++) {\n    hash ^= value.charCodeAt(i);\n    hash = Math.imul(hash, 0x01000193);\n  }\n  return (hash >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, '0');\n}\n\nfunction observationFingerprint(observation: ToolLoopObservation): string {\n  const input = JSON.stringify(stableValue(observation.input));\n  const images = observation.images.map(hashText).join(',');\n  return `${observation.name}:${hashText(input)}:${hashText(observation.result)}:${images}:${observation.error ? The no-progress guard catches a degenerate spin in\n * MAX_NO_PROGRESS_TURNS, so this cap only needs to bound the rarer \"well-formed but\n * unproductive\" loop — generous is fine.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 200;\n\n/**\n * Resolve the per-run turn cap.
